points.description: States that a fixed mass of one element combines with different masses of another element to form compounds (mass data from the Law of Multiple Proportions).
points.partial_credit: 1 mark if only one of fixed mass or varying masses/compound formation is stated.

points.description: States that the masses of the second element are in a simple whole-number (integer) ratio, and that whole-number ratios mean matter combines in indivisible (discrete) units, not in arbitrary amounts.
points.partial_credit: 1.5 marks if the whole-number ratio is stated but the link to indivisible units is not made; 1 mark if only 'whole numbers' is stated with no link to indivisibility.

points.description: Concludes that the indivisible unit of mass is the atom, so matter must be made of atoms.
points.partial_credit: 1.5 marks if 'atom' is named but not stated as the indivisible unit that makes up matter; 1 mark for a bare claim that matter is made of atoms with no link to the ratio data.

rubric.notes: Full marks need the fixed-mass compound data, the whole-number ratio, the inference that whole numbers mean indivisible units, and the conclusion that the indivisible unit is the atom. Part marks go to a half-stated link or a vague claim, as shown in each point. A statement of the law without the inference to indivisible units, or a bare definition of atoms, earns no marks for that point. Wrong statements (for example, that the ratio shows atoms are divisible) lose that point's marks only.
